bull.b: COMPASS has a large, late-stage dataset—over 1,000 patients and replicated 26-week durability—which materially de-risks efficacy claims versus earlier-stage peers. Durable, blinded follow-up strengthens approval prospects, payer conversations and clinician confidence over the next 2–6 months.

A rolling NDA combined with a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher meaningfully shortens regulatory timeline risk if final data are acceptable. This structural acceleration improves predictability for launch planning and reduces timing uncertainty compared with a standard review clock.

Recent financings and warrant exercises provide multi-year runway and the company carries minimal debt, giving financial flexibility to complete filing, build commercial infrastructure and support initial launch activities without immediate refinancing pressure.

bear.b: COMPASS remains pre-revenue with materially negative operating and free cash flow (TTM FCF ~ -$160M and TTM EBIT ~ -$172M). Sustained cash burn makes the business dependent on external capital until commercial revenues stabilize, constraining long-term self-funding ability.

Balance-sheet swings—equity briefly negative in 2025—signal prior dilution and the company’s reliance on financings to sustain R&D and commercial build. Such capital dependence increases dilution risk for shareholders and can complicate long-term planning if commercialization costs rise.

Key structural risks persist: final Part B data are required to complete the filing, REMS/DEA rescheduling sequencing is unresolved, CPT codes are still Category III and RUC/CMS valuation plus payer negotiations remain open. These execution points could delay access and uptake post-approval.
